## Natural history notes

A small burrowing mammal characterized by its cylindrical body, velvety gray to brown fur, pointed snout, tiny eyes, and broad front feet adapted for digging. In Florida, it is found in sandy or loose soils in habitats such as pine flatwoods, fields, lawns, gardens, pastures, and open woodlands. It spends most of its life underground, creating shallow tunnels while feeding mainly on earthworms, insects, and other soil invertebrates.
